# The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Context · hash: sha256:37861e2e14013ad7c69dfa0ecab17370a0a0e6cf9631382cdc23dff2fa1ba904*

## Context

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Context · hash: sha256:b16d1367a942161c8515f7f15d1ccf7a18099c2bfcb2a7deae83a9acdda21ff1*

The Nomos specification existed as roughly twenty versioned archives of markdown. The
latest of them, v15.0, is a reorganization of v14.36 that destroyed content: 132 files
hold placeholder prose, 282 markdown table rows and all 6 code blocks are gone, and with
them the entire canonical domain model, all 8 roadmap release definitions, all 8 worked
scenarios and all 54 service descriptions.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Context · hash: sha256:d62069725b0daebcea923f3ad2eadcc8d2b8a0af4436ff4ff44a4e0930f5245e*

The mechanism that would have caught this already existed. v14 shipped a per-block hash
manifest under a policy named `blocks_are_not_silently_dropped_from_source`, and a bundle
validator that implements the heading-disposition check. v15.0 shipped the normalized
views, deleted the narrative, and ran none of it. A publication gate had already been
declared for exactly this case.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Context · hash: sha256:041aceff2e4386117b8fb4fbe0b7947e5694420986ee1d0c90200a8c714a9feb*

The failure was not a missing check. It was that nothing forced the check to run, and a
run that checked nothing was indistinguishable from a run that found nothing wrong.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Decision · hash: sha256:a15c7c13f167e5ac9204c02acb3f22d9fffdadf996618ee0e068a4b27e4c1511*

## Decision

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Decision · hash: sha256:f197b6249d6ad4d9a72608c16ac37116d5e7a6165808db0c50cb90645fc2228a*

The specification is a database. Content is addressed by hash, identity is a stable
`node_id`, and `uid` is a join surrogate that never leaves the process. Markdown, YAML,
JSON and HTML become generated projections of that store.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Decision · hash: sha256:f85976042b48666d8c0abe7c5ce0477ccdc0076886eb5e88b7a2ac0aa4aac39f*

Every source document is segmented into blocks, and every block carries both its verbatim
hash and its normalized hash. Every block and every heading must have a recorded
disposition or a recorded omission. An omission carries a reason, a justification and a
decision record, and is itself validated.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Decision · hash: sha256:8ffa40fc89e03ea470de8b0df8aeb48ca3f62637bd9ce7424d245a97a793a86c*

A validation run passes only when every declared rule ran to completion. A declared rule
with no implementation, a registered rule the manifest never declared, and a rule that
errored internally all fail the run. The absence of a validator must be indistinguishable
from a failing one.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Decision · hash: sha256:5c9eee28252b6fba1fe3ff8db3f9b30c54d1f28b8c914d80c250a7ee762d72db*

A satisfied rule records how many subjects it examined, because "0 violations over 0
subjects" and "0 violations over 2533 subjects" print the same and mean opposite things.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Consequences · hash: sha256:89452c3c3f042e75cb1c74f2df2a941f9dbbbad6127f3d11c1fb606337059416*

## Consequences

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Consequences · hash: sha256:be65c9b8c52b3a2bd90e1b98cab06380ed5a16ca67b6981452e18c136dd3e442*

Content cannot leave silently. It can still leave — through an omission that names a
decision record — which is what keeps the gate a gate rather than a wall.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Consequences · hash: sha256:8889f5f53086e9bd24ec99ed1c9797627677bb62ffe5949098fbfac4506c2c11*

The portable authority committed to git is a deterministic JSONL bundle rather than the
database file. A bundle round trip is byte-identical, so the corpus can be reviewed as a
diff.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Consequences · hash: sha256:dfd2266cf8a45edddb217cbbfbcb5e2e8a077f3fe96719b624680de11e034fd5*

Generated documentation is never committed and never becomes source. Five independent
barriers enforce that, because one barrier is a convention.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:4824749d250c30ac7d0d3b75dd866d8a845308adcba154f5372cf74980c63d83*

## Alternatives Considered

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:cfc30e8af580b3e1e7c3fe50ca6aeac507f6a0d8fc4722e93527f53bfc9ecf29*

Keeping markdown as the identity substrate and adding a stricter validator was rejected.
That is what v14 already had, and it did not survive one reorganization, because the
validator was a step somebody had to remember rather than a property of the store.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:e3e9ae60881fa382fe98c2e8bd4963a441403992177b9b30173f2344ea55a457*

Storing only the normalized view was rejected. It is what v15.0 did. A normalized view is
never a replacement for either source authority, and the 282 rows lost are what that
sentence costs when it is advice instead of a constraint.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-001-the-specification-is-a-database.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification is a database with an enforced preservation ledger / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:8ab3f76a9e983cd71305ba33a2c6f1d7da533e3f3fe33abf2a47e875553a5328*

Rebuilding from the archives by hand was rejected. Without a per-block ledger there is no
way to tell restoration from invention.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#1

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content · hash: sha256:d06aefaf6adb2631ff43fbdc878eb11ede9dc3f3dfc3f78d50cbf07f1e5102a6*

# A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Question · hash: sha256:6b8674b82694cad849134fafcdef47988068953168874a87637cb2c6fc599ec7*

This repository holds two kinds of thing and has one rule for both.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Question · hash: sha256:d82071d03bfb940e1d26a7297f66a588f61e00d2b9e2dfd4e0b7d047d6a1536a*

`ARC-SPECDB-001` says the specification is a database. `OD-SPEC-006` says the markdown files
under `docs/records` remain the substrate this repository authors in, and gives evidential
grounds: nothing persists a specification database, the store is assembled on every
invocation, so what survives an invocation is the file.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Question · hash: sha256:28e7319a7a0194461e84332d7ff5392f481a7f6739ba651f0507bc9b556e30f4*

Neither says which objects belong on which side, because until now every object was on the
same side. That is no longer true. A typed feature-request layer is being designed whose
content is a set of answers to questions that exist before anybody answers them, and the
question of where such an object lives has been argued twice with no rule to argue from.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Question · hash: sha256:95840efb317403555a4bb0f8c4764f7a6e5a8a578c053a58de84556c07ff38c0*

`P10-CANONICITY-DECISION` recorded the strongest form of the objection in its abandonment:
deciding this per artifact would put two substrates in one build and encode the split in the
schema of every typed row. That objection is correct and it is fatal to a split drawn on
**artifact kind**. It says nothing about a split drawn on a property the objects themselves
have. The difference between those two axes is what has never been written down, and this
record writes it down rather than deciding any particular object.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / The Rule · hash: sha256:4865a77f8126915a6ad3e6a258f5af73eefc1b30baeb4938ea003d7b90eeeae5*

## The Rule

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / The Rule · hash: sha256:50f9a3778e5b15a242fa30d38c0e91551e6a0059e99186e8371bc86442ca08ee*

> An object is **born structured** when its schema can be stated before its content exists.
> Its canonical form is the structured record, and every document is a projection of that
> record.
>
> An object is **document-first** when its content exists before any schema can describe it.
> Its canonical form is the document, and the store holds a derived index of it.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / The Rule · hash: sha256:9a4ce0f4f0c8a3899e72b97487693fd8c00c60e2c6586eedbbd40eef2c8ec972*

The test is not who wrote the object, nor when, nor which directory it currently sits in. It
is whether a schema written in advance can be filled in without deciding, at fill-in time,
what the fields should have been.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / The Rule · hash: sha256:f4dcc784026f5a6ee1dcfd1c80a1d7dcc0ae6ef83553e3611e3f37886f230e0e*

That test is answerable about an object nobody has proposed yet, which is the property this
rule exists to have. A reader with a new object asks one question: can I write the form
before I know the answer? If yes, the record is canonical and the markdown is generated. If
no, the document is canonical and the rows index it.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Why The Artifact-Kind Axis Is Refused · hash: sha256:868764192c1afab0df20523b39147dd250a62ef34d377572959a6942daeaf0e5*

## Why The Artifact-Kind Axis Is Refused

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Why The Artifact-Kind Axis Is Refused · hash: sha256:326e83275fea5a26fa5e79b87f7ee882cd19a53fd970082f7911a5ab5e87c45a*

A rule of the form *feature requests live in the store, governing records live in files* is
refused, and refused rather than merely not chosen.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Why The Artifact-Kind Axis Is Refused · hash: sha256:b137f06a74b181f3a90bb39a0abef0702b7efd551627a5f18c4da3b64e320736*

It is a list, not a rule. It answers for the objects on the list and produces nothing for the
next object, so every addition reopens the question and is settled by whoever is holding the
pen. That is the second-authority failure this repository is organised against, and it would
be installed in the schema of every typed row rather than in a document somebody could read
and disagree with.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Why The Artifact-Kind Axis Is Refused · hash: sha256:90e282632bffda17b987eda8b376bbf6a6de9f863d706f56b6f4ce32dab46327*

It also cannot be checked. A rule about a property of the object can be applied by a reader
and got wrong visibly. A list can only be consulted, and a list that has fallen behind looks
exactly like a list that is complete.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Why The Artifact-Kind Axis Is Refused · hash: sha256:c59cf2736bac1c3f74df80e3f00d0591050275880e19739041e6aed620cf54b5*

The provenance framing — *born here versus imported* — is closer, and is still wrong. A
governing record is born here and is not born structured. Origin is a fact about who typed
it; what decides the substrate is whether the thing typed had a shape before it was typed.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What Each Side Owes · hash: sha256:20c302b7d5ecb875ae8e98cd3d988477737f92f703301f30b9fa47045d53c7e3*

## What Each Side Owes

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What Each Side Owes · hash: sha256:1bfdb3ed5fb9f09968abf4c90d99115f731f2c804f21347dd10ae8966701271a*

The two substrates are not two standards of care. Each side pays for what the other side's
machinery gives it for free, and the exchange is stated here so that neither is later read as
the cheap option.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What Each Side Owes · hash: sha256:251aeab8383629fd2c724dc897d836eaa2e98a99812968e7556489def880cc2a*

A **born-structured** object skips the preservation and round-trip machinery, because there
is no arbitrary document to prove recoverable — the fields were fields when they were
written. In exchange it owes four things:

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What Each Side Owes · hash: sha256:6da32ea810875630f6925b95b51b219b5561eacdb1d94ac16f7cab9011c8513f*

- a declared schema carrying its own version, so a record written under an older shape is
  readable as that shape rather than silently reinterpreted;
- validation at write time, refusing an incomplete submission rather than accepting it and
  relying on a later reader to notice what is missing;
- separation of what was originally submitted from what was later clarified, inferred or
  decided, so that the two are never merged into one field that no longer says which it is;
- a freshness obligation on every committed projection, because the moment a generated
  document is committed it can disagree with the record it came from.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What Each Side Owes · hash: sha256:e061463b8719af3a6634749fe931fe72cde8233d5a35da6a51bba4a577c21df9*

That last item is the exchange stated plainly: a born-structured object trades a
**round-trip proof** for a **freshness proof**. It is not exempt from proof. `OD-SPEC-006`
already names the same obligation for the other direction, and the gate already runs one
freshness step.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What Each Side Owes · hash: sha256:75e4204bd505a2a294a85ee583626d1e0ce332dfd9eced3a9843f45b2a77bd5e*

A **document-first** object keeps the machinery `ARC-SPECDB-001` exists for: every block
accounted for by a disposition, every statement traced to its source, and any content that
leaves recorded as an omission with a justification pointing at a decision. It owes that
because nothing else can establish what it contained.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What This Rule Does Not Change · hash: sha256:537ea83b80567c7c940e457c1f8c6b04acaef094f097b35670931a2e580b8fbb*

## What This Rule Does Not Change

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What This Rule Does Not Change · hash: sha256:f3b542c335a69f9ee68feb7084d66d2cddfaaf020edda175fc4c402585730eb3*

It does not amend `OD-SPEC-006`, and reading it as an amendment would be wrong.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#24

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What This Rule Does Not Change · hash: sha256:2194d0aae1ee11936119a67f110d575094deb392459f6edcb8134103244a736e*

`OD-SPEC-006` reaches the document-first outcome for governing records on evidential grounds
— that nothing persists a specification database today. This rule reaches the same outcome
for those records on structural grounds: a governing record is an argument, and the argument
is the artifact. There are no fields to fill in, because the shape of the case is not known
until the case is made. Rendering such a record from fields would lose the thing it was
written for.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What This Rule Does Not Change · hash: sha256:23f76e3391b7ddf9247af22398b8f51665646d58461f344c0c1de048e7edcbc8*

The two grounds are independent and agree, which is worth saying because they have different
lifetimes. If the evidential ground ever changes — if the store becomes durable and the seed
stops compiling the files into the binary — the structural ground still holds, and governing
records stay document-first for a reason that no infrastructure change can retire.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#26

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What This Rule Does Not Change · hash: sha256:3a670e9f04bf2cb0dcaee6fcaea93047a20f447ea7196cf72569eb928d09ccd6*

It does not decide anything about feature requests, designs or results. Those are objects
this rule can be applied to, and applying it is a separate decision with its own record.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#27

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / What This Rule Does Not Change · hash: sha256:8823b0983c1bba94de833041796a52329a9adffe051da5e293430192cae5d0c1*

It does not license a second substrate on demand. Two substrates exist here because two
kinds of object exist, and a proposal for a third substrate is a claim that a third kind of
object exists, which has to be argued on this axis or not at all.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#28

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Consequences · hash: sha256:89452c3c3f042e75cb1c74f2df2a941f9dbbbad6127f3d11c1fb606337059416*

## Consequences

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#29

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Consequences · hash: sha256:cc93c03ed58bf42dd8c21cda0335d4b4f794597ca7ab1de1bec4658056cbfa9b*

The next substrate question is answered by reading this record rather than by re-arguing
`OD-SPEC-006` from its evidence, which is what the last two attempts did.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#30

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Consequences · hash: sha256:d0a5ae89c60167c26a39b3161adf717444f659b39ace3b03516fcb598300fb65*

An object that fails the test in one direction and is placed in the other is now a defect
somebody can name, rather than a preference somebody exercised.

### docs/records/ARC-SPECDB-002-a-canonical-substrate-is-decided-by-whether-the-schema-precedes-the-content.md#31

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A canonical substrate is decided by whether the schema precedes the content / Consequences · hash: sha256:1419bfbb7613054e9edd595cacea3d383b04c2234a22b3eb9fc2aaee06ce08ab*

The preservation machinery stops being the universal tax it currently looks like. It is what
document-first objects owe, and the work of proving that arbitrary markdown round-trips is
not owed by an object that was never arbitrary markdown.

# The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Decision · hash: sha256:a15c7c13f167e5ac9204c02acb3f22d9fffdadf996618ee0e068a4b27e4c1511*

## Decision

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Decision · hash: sha256:82b56c54c76d9f0bed761bd9ccbd1a57ca2526b296916c2b709416c982784444*

The specification store holds identity. A `node_id` is stable across databases and travels
in a bundle; a file path is navigation and may change without changing what a thing is.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Decision · hash: sha256:14340adf0780becbc8d72c54551659f2a03f287b8d5c8e092614d1da04d3a068*

Markdown remains the surface people author through, via a round trip that reads a record
out as markdown and writes the edit back. It stops being the substrate in which identity
lives.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Decision · hash: sha256:b652e192b5e7dc5962f705db4a923768e0c222743e096f35439186b53e3bd79f*

This supersedes ADR-DOC-001, which made markdown files with constrained YAML front matter
the canonical authored source.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Rationale · hash: sha256:e0682f7fa92faabf4e7019619e38e5c354daf233cff6ff3f9b1890a8982bb2db*

## Rationale

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Rationale · hash: sha256:3a5d1944080935ad414a147660494f0c42aeb3d07963f7af43899d80d27ded35*

ADR-DOC-001 was right about prose. Architecture rationale, requirements, tradeoffs and
open questions are explanatory text, markdown represents them directly, and diffs stay
reviewable. None of that is disputed here and none of it is being reversed — markdown is
still what an author types.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Rationale · hash: sha256:7cd412c52b5ed64b374634ba3fc766d89ebcf748cc994f557edf06b6058da388*

What ADR-DOC-001 could not give is a place for the relationship between two revisions of
the same content to live. It says "every important authored artifact needs a stable ID and
typed relations", and that is exactly the requirement a filesystem cannot enforce: a file
tree has no way to refuse a reorganization that drops 282 rows, because at the file level
nothing was dropped. v15.0 satisfied every constraint ADR-DOC-001 states and still lost the
content.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Rationale · hash: sha256:9a2b103bd2883e8c878358d17ee58d3a9abef8496335bc8720c7e58c2d92acfb*

Leaving both records live would leave two answers to what the source of truth is, so this
one names the supersession explicitly rather than quietly disagreeing.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Consequences · hash: sha256:89452c3c3f042e75cb1c74f2df2a941f9dbbbad6127f3d11c1fb606337059416*

## Consequences

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Consequences · hash: sha256:7a3928caad62f06e11fb3c39eb7b7fdba5b4af4f67c8cc775779e05e5576cf3a*

Identity survives renames, and a rename is an ordinary edit rather than a migration.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Consequences · hash: sha256:1f5fded58027697a59cd8cc8486669b37ef05d3d0472eb311cc965ba25f3cd84*

An author still edits markdown, but the edit is a transaction against the store: claim,
stage, preview, commit. The preview is mandatory and names what the edit changes,
including whether normative wording moved.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / Consequences · hash: sha256:4be281b70627b045eb5515a492d1fd4058b12c21c8a7024c9e972fca328de806*

ADR-DOC-001 stays in the store as a superseded node. Its prose is restored from the v14
corpus in Phase 3; until then it is present by identity and by this edge, not by content.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#14

## What Is Not Built (amended at version 2)

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Not Built (amended at version 2) · hash: sha256:49018f6d3dc9f93fa8de64d38d3ac083898fa5211268bc69835f0697963604dd*

*Answered by the version 3 section below. Kept as written, because the gap it records is what
made the work schedulable and a record that quietly stops mentioning its own gap teaches
nobody anything.*

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Not Built (amended at version 2) · hash: sha256:9aefaeecd66c19654254017098d73a4ad2986ed20e6024aa4cbd6132a6281dc3*

The round trip does not exist. Nothing reads a record out of the store as markdown, and
nothing writes an edit back. There is no claim, stage, preview or commit against the store
for an authored record; the preview this record calls mandatory has never run.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Not Built (amended at version 2) · hash: sha256:93996ee33f0d2fda112522f85c607999053bcd3fe8342dd3cd12cd62e4edcec3*

So the second paragraph of the decision describes an intent, and until now it read as a
description of the system. That is the specific failure mode this whole build is organised
against — a governing record asserting a capability, validated, in the store, and nothing
exercising it — and the honest correction is to say so in the record rather than to leave a
reader to discover it from the absence of a command.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Not Built (amended at version 2) · hash: sha256:f7f729102fcc93b06220d001e8b3c8c5b2e32d0a3ed912dc4e6f997f3b704511*

What is built is the first paragraph, and it is load-bearing: the store holds identity, a
`node_id` is stable across databases and travels in a bundle, and `P3-*` restored content
against those identities across five revisions. Nothing here is retracted. The supersession
of ADR-DOC-001 stands, because it is about where identity lives and not about how an author
types.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Not Built (amended at version 2) · hash: sha256:4f41a2191081543154f947a4527946d68defaecaffa8edc6e34bf4398f101f2d*

What follows from the gap, and is the reason it is worth recording rather than merely
fixing: **markdown files under `docs/records` are still the substrate in practice.** These
records are authored as files, seeded into the store from those files by `include_str!`, and
edited as files. The store holds a copy. Identity is stable because the seed says so, not
because an authoring transaction ever produced it — and the direction of that dependency is
the opposite of what this record decides.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Not Built (amended at version 2) · hash: sha256:715fdfac8bdecb00e6461476dc2a1a775e3c23fbcbafc806c0d4ade5c8feec1d*

`P9-AUTHORING` carries the round trip. It is a phase of work rather than a defect to patch,
and stating the gap is what makes it schedulable.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Built (amended at version 3) · hash: sha256:1d7ed437979c8f06c0d3b03d7b67a1b52677475e63f698962712968129cc5b82*

## What Is Built (amended at version 3)

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Built (amended at version 3) · hash: sha256:4650d4532714aaaa35f7f4b5cdce0a12f855e20f2cb98d10ac918dfdf1d5f923*

The round trip exists. `nomos spec markdown` renders a record out of the store's own rows —
the declared front matter and the block rows, never the ingested blob — and `nomos spec
preview` and `nomos spec commit` write an edit back as one transaction. The preview is
mandatory in the only way that survives a careless caller: committing takes a preview value
that nothing outside the module can construct, so an unpreviewed commit is not a lapse of
discipline but an unwritable program. The preview names whether normative wording moved, from
the normalizer over the blocks and from the recorded statements where a corpus has supplied
them, and says which of the two it used.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Built (amended at version 3) · hash: sha256:30542dbb0028429162a2b21fe0cef4df7e404ce10d7a60afbb0da76491203598*

Identity survives the round trip, and a rename is an ordinary edit: the document row is
updated rather than replaced, so the block surrogates every lineage row hangs from are
untouched, and retyping `id:` in a staged file is refused because identity is not a property
of the file.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#24

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Built (amended at version 3) · hash: sha256:6a7779dc768feb8a702e97f60600aae9fd1fca5318b2bc4156fb5511b8d30572*

What this does not do is move the substrate, and that half is now recorded rather than
implied. Markdown files under `docs/records` are still what this repository authors in,
because nothing persists a specification database: the store is assembled per invocation from
records compiled into the binary. `OD-SPEC-006` states that on the evidence, says what would
have to change for the store to become durable, and names the obstacle already recorded
against the obvious route.

### docs/records/D-129-the-store-is-the-identity-substrate.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The specification store is the identity substrate; markdown is an editing surface / What Is Built (amended at version 3) · hash: sha256:7563e49767188868da14821c4a294ee68b9cb0fd27dcb7d6d7193c7c8527b22d*

So the second paragraph of the decision now describes the system. What changed underneath it
is the evidence rather than the dependency: the store used to hold a copy of unknown
fidelity, and it now holds a projection asserted byte for byte, in both directions, over every
record in it.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#1

# Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Decision · hash: sha256:a15c7c13f167e5ac9204c02acb3f22d9fffdadf996618ee0e068a4b27e4c1511*

## Decision

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Decision · hash: sha256:20f6c9a1d1f7b3e62e683b85eed6d2c3709b632060008d4124a983b2595d6ee6*

No Nomos crate depends on the sibling XVPE workspace before Phase 5. The platform port
traits exist from Phase 0, so adopting an XVPE implementation later is a new implementation
behind an existing seam rather than a refactor.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Decision · hash: sha256:8ae4dfeff72f253863b68113bec001fe23431ebbf2d3c6e4193e1b641eb55a18*

When adoption happens it is by git reference and commit SHA into one quarantined crate,
`nomos-platform-xvpe`. It is never a `path` dependency.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Rationale · hash: sha256:e0682f7fa92faabf4e7019619e38e5c354daf233cff6ff3f9b1890a8982bb2db*

## Rationale

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Rationale · hash: sha256:b13d99f9915ecf44d589e72380bc0bbfc18882dcf97db1ae525bf5c6e9e457f9*

XVPE does not currently compile. Its own error log ends with a dataflow crate failing on
62 errors, and the in-flight refactor is concentrated in exactly the crates Nomos would
want: dataflow, scheduling, serialization. A `path` dependency would make Nomos's
buildability a function of another product's refactor.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Rationale · hash: sha256:e3e0ae5ba1e9ee5e56f87acbfbbc61ae7de8506652c2e48450ded8fd5971d37a*

Several crates that sound reusable are not. `xvpe-composer-headless` is an offscreen GPU
renderer, so "headless" there means "no window system" rather than "no graphics", and
depending on it would put a GPU stack under a command-line tool. `xvpe-telemetry` pulls a
desktop OS backend. `xvpe-replay` is game-world rewind. There is no storage crate and no
package crate; those are specified rather than built.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Rationale · hash: sha256:1aaf75b1bb378b655f62a9858b57cf2de62c1b8665751bd1dafb2be4187e8868*

A commit SHA is the difference between adopting a body of work and adopting whatever that
work becomes.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Consequences · hash: sha256:89452c3c3f042e75cb1c74f2df2a941f9dbbbad6127f3d11c1fb606337059416*

## Consequences

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Consequences · hash: sha256:bd9d2ca045e588a2ec305e92ede234310111c23f86d5631d7cece258b038fd33*

`deny.toml` bans the GPU, windowing and UI crates on the default feature set, so a headless
build cannot acquire them transitively even by accident.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Consequences · hash: sha256:6f9a5c069dc8712281bb6cf7e029bd659d547bd997a1b050d2d2fefe33f712fb*

A boundary test asserts that only `nomos-platform-xvpe` may name anything beginning with
`xvpe-`. That crate does not exist yet; naming it in the test now means the exception is a
decision somebody wrote down rather than a line added later to make a failing test pass.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Consequences · hash: sha256:f2dc5e095ee3f8bbb7c11b7ddb6fa7b5fb856bbe5ff5e653b40974828e092d90*

Genuine candidates stay identified rather than forgotten: hazard detection over read and
write sets, cycle witnesses over strongly connected components, dirty propagation and
topological layering for fact invalidation, and the graph algorithms.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:4824749d250c30ac7d0d3b75dd866d8a845308adcba154f5372cf74980c63d83*

## Alternatives Considered

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:ef1999020112bb5071e7bbbcd06f29c850f48cc7e7d5348aa2a72a37620c5309*

Vendoring the wanted algorithms was rejected for now. It creates a fork with no upstream
path, and the algorithms are not yet on any critical path.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:ad7818690ce0542ea1cf0176ae4fea5ef39f2ca8e052bd8ab375f8901446f290*

Waiting for XVPE to stabilize before starting Nomos was rejected. The port traits make the
dependency optional, so there is nothing to wait for.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Amendment: The Build-Instability Premise Resolved; The Gate Did Not · hash: sha256:0882ecd2b4c1e4078bd15e5d11267ee347712f8ac85d6cc433b492c08f010534*

## Amendment: The Build-Instability Premise Resolved; The Gate Did Not

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Amendment: The Build-Instability Premise Resolved; The Gate Did Not · hash: sha256:90b1c95ccdcaa37e5297f565cfee50715b56dde7e42f8314956a5d111e9f0577*

The rationale above cited a specific, dated fact: a dataflow crate failing on 62 errors,
with the in-flight refactor concentrated in dataflow, scheduling and serialization.
Checked directly against xvpe dev at commit `557dada32ed0c33c7c2fde09b5320d3fdbc94d91`,
`cargo check -p xvpe-dataflow -p xvpe-scheduling -p xvpe-task-host -p xvpe-clock -p
xvpe-serialization` succeeds, warnings only. All five crates compile clean, including the
three this record named as blocking. The genuine candidates already identified above live
inside them: `hazard_detector.rs`, `cycle_witness.rs` and `topological.rs` sit in
`xvpe-scheduling`; dirty propagation sits in `xvpe-dataflow`. The specific instability this
record was written against no longer describes the tree.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Amendment: The Build-Instability Premise Resolved; The Gate Did Not · hash: sha256:1a8bf1ecc687135a7869ccdde0a62d1252fa80523dab8d150194a063aa074ff2*

That does not lift the gate, because two of this record's other conditions are unchanged
and neither is a build-stability question. xvpe's workspace — 112 members at this
commit — still contains no storage crate and no package crate; a clean compile cannot
adopt a crate that was never written. `xvpe-telemetry`'s `Cargo.toml` still names
`xvpe-os-backend-desktop` as a direct dependency, exactly as it did when this record was
accepted. A third fact sharpens the same point rather than adding a new one: xvpe as a
whole is organized as `crates/engine/{foundations,simulation,runtime,presentation}` —
rendering, audio, physics, animation, camera, HUD, materials and scene crates sit beside
the ones Nomos would actually want, inside one workspace. A `path` dependency does not
select the crates that happen to compile today; it selects the workspace, and this is a
full game engine's workspace, not a narrow platform library's.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Amendment: The Build-Instability Premise Resolved; The Gate Did Not · hash: sha256:5938429190dec85c620e216ac5feadc479d24a991847254211f41383da0f6c22*

The phase gate is therefore not narrowed to a compile-stability condition on the named
crates. Compiling is necessary — an XVPE that does not build would be disqualified on that
fact alone — but this reverification is the demonstration that it is not sufficient: the
exact crates this record called out now compile cleanly, and the record's other reasons to
wait are untouched by that. Phase 5 stands as the gate, unconditioned on whichever phase
number the tree happens to be build-stable at, because what Phase 5 is waiting for — a
storage crate, a package crate, and an adoption path that does not pull a desktop OS
backend or a rendering engine in behind it — is not a fact about whether `cargo check`
currently exits zero.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#20

## Amendment: The Adapter Count Was Retired; The Path Clause And The Phase Gate Were Not

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Amendment: The Adapter Count Was Retired; The Path Clause And The Phase Gate Were Not · hash: sha256:101fd1c696284177a10bc4647fa62e160702edb028803975c45280485262bd86*

This record made two mechanical decisions about the XVPE crossing, and only one of them has
been retired. Read together they looked like a single rule, which is how the other came to
lapse without anybody deciding that it should.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Amendment: The Adapter Count Was Retired; The Path Clause And The Phase Gate Were Not · hash: sha256:69059eb0978be59ccd7fa64b6a1fa79b2a78fd062ccc89ced9d240d30d40648f*

**What was retired.** The boundary test this record's Consequences section describes is gone.
`Test_Only_The_Platform_Adapter_May_Name_The_Sibling_Workspace` does not resolve: it was
removed on 2026-09-10 by the owner's decision, and `tests/contract/tests/boundaries/graph.rs`
carries the tombstone where it stood. What it enforced was an adapter *count* — that exactly
one named crate may reach an `xvpe-` dependency. `OD-PLATFORM-003` holds the reasoning: nomos
is built on top of XVPE as the knowledge workbench is, XVPE is the engine and this workspace
an application over it, so a rule forbidding that dependency does not describe an architecture
worth keeping. The tombstone records why it was retired rather than widened — an allow-list of
nine crates would have left a rule that still reads as a boundary while enforcing nothing,
which is worse than no rule.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#24

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Amendment: The Adapter Count Was Retired; The Path Clause And The Phase Gate Were Not · hash: sha256:00ce583d58c280999c79eb42e6f2901c02581111cb188de13744b1c5cf48d4e1*

**That retirement is accepted, and this record's quarantine clause is withdrawn with it.** More
than one crate here may name `xvpe-`, and `nomos-platform-xvpe` is no longer the sole permitted
crossing.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Amendment: The Adapter Count Was Retired; The Path Clause And The Phase Gate Were Not · hash: sha256:8430aaeb33c33e73bad2fd1a44be835f6f80da7d997043fdb32335ef0d0f41e5*

**What was not retired.** Two clauses survive, and neither is a claim about how many crates may
cross.

### docs/records/D-130-no-xvpe-dependency-before-phase-5.md#26

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path / Amendment: The Adapter Count Was Retired; The Path Clause And The Phase Gate Were Not · hash: sha256:76cfaa3b0dd5319ea165638eaa4031cd1de4b318352897b4f9e094efbf1ff806*

The first is the *form* of the dependency: adoption is "by git reference and commit SHA", and
"never a `path` dependency". Retiring the quarantine did not decide the pinning. They answer
different questions — one asks how many crates may cross, the other asks whether this
workspace's buildability and reproducibility are a function of another product's working tree
at whatever revision that tree happens to be sitting at, with nothing recording which revision
that was. The second question's answer does not change with the number of crossings, so
nothing about the 2026-09-10 decision reaches it.

deliberately. It is not superseded here.

# A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / Decision · hash: sha256:a15c7c13f167e5ac9204c02acb3f22d9fffdadf996618ee0e068a4b27e4c1511*

## Decision

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / Decision · hash: sha256:774d745d02cd64b22c0cf946035cd606ad1c3dd83b778d4bbaa4dd9a0fd3b5b6*

`Segment` recognises an optional leading byte order mark as part of a document's opening
front matter fence. Where front matter follows, the mark leaves with it and reaches no
block. Where none follows, the mark is kept in the text exactly as found.

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / Why It Had To Be Settled First · hash: sha256:f4b9facd2c050e2c47886e89ab942447369329bb867a52ccec1d7952732b36f8*

## Why It Had To Be Settled First

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / Why It Had To Be Settled First · hash: sha256:8d7a0f0a0808441ddbdac8760a85864ea22233b4cc085cb011737edd63c2fe75*

1637 of the 2187 authored v14 documents carry a mark, including all six decision records
and every artifact under `01_authoring/artifacts`. `str::trim` does not remove one —
U+FEFF is not whitespace under Unicode — so the first line of a marked document did not
compare equal to `---` and its front matter was segmented as prose. I4 ingests exactly
those documents through `Ingest_Source_Document`, which segments raw file text.

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / Why It Had To Be Settled First · hash: sha256:f8abee23b9c828434ec90d7ee481045e674f45cc2a7e6e05a764ec1762788109*

Every block hash downstream depends on the answer, and the P1 gate rests on reproducing
v14's hashes. Guessing would have moved them.

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / The Evidence · hash: sha256:4304963d62d201a473a5dcdfdc689cf14aa577c87c2932120e97ceaa34a5f125*

## The Evidence

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / The Evidence · hash: sha256:0a91fcb23999205346d019a99212f848d718831eb6d72dbe96fa29e7fba23692*

Both v14 readers that ship compile the same pattern:

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: code · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / The Evidence · hash: sha256:c603c407efc12d0fd60ef9e45e5143d1ebf4a63c8b08ee3eb3452d9a3fc5b698*

```python
FRONT_RE = re.compile(r'^\ufeff?---\n(.*?)\n---\n', re.S)
```

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / The Evidence · hash: sha256:ea82851cb654a1cf41c60b464c4f7d979a5f419ee2723cf5389537ee160231c3*

`build_spec.py::split_markdown_front_matter` and
`validate_bundle.py::markdown_document_records` each read with `encoding='utf-8'`, which
leaves the mark in the string, and each match with that pattern, which consumes it.

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / The Evidence · hash: sha256:f77b122da485ed058ad00829c6c777e577d979eee1e21c896750031df4268a9f*

Run over the archives, the pattern matches all 2187 authored documents — 1637 marked, 550
not — with no exception in either direction, and no body retains a mark. The negative case
is what makes it conclusive: `markdown_document_records` walks the whole authoring tree and
reports `missing YAML front matter` on any document it cannot match. Had the mark not been
tolerated, v14 would have reported 1637 such errors. It validated clean.

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / What The Archives Do Not Settle · hash: sha256:bacef1e5bf9365eb3b3633ac4cd31f09b280d522bb778f634ac2f914954079fa*

## What The Archives Do Not Settle

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / What The Archives Do Not Settle · hash: sha256:8075974ad872a090eeb338e42bfcb995cc869b2a659f546d1d903bc12964199f*

`source-block-lineage.yaml` records 2533 blocks drawn from exactly ten documents, the
domain volumes, and **none of the ten carries a mark**. No recorded block hash corroborates
any of this, and the segmenter that produced those hashes does not ship with the corpus.

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / What The Archives Do Not Settle · hash: sha256:7e990d595a73d64e30765080805624bdf32721c9a4417e13a05d01711c83a096*

So the authority here is the two readers' agreement, not the manifest. This is recorded
rather than resolved by preference, and it is the reason the decision is stated as a
decision instead of as a reproduction.

### docs/records/D-131-a-byte-order-mark-belongs-to-the-front-matter-fence.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A byte order mark belongs to the front matter fence / What The Archives Do Not Settle · hash: sha256:bea1693d2facb5d0246789ee5fc1c5bc7f49962873aace6bbaf09a0ed4799d8c*

The second branch — a marked document with no front matter — occurs zero times in the
corpus and is therefore settled by faithfulness to what v14's reader did rather than by
evidence: no fence matched, so it dropped nothing. Keeping the mark is also the only
choice consistent with a preservation ledger, because the sole bytes discarded are a
delimiter's.

## Decision

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / Decision · hash: sha256:90e6bdc42174c4f7571e7086e32643584a9f1e843b56dc8ed5e75191f000e8a6*

**D-120 extends to the plan document.** It is lineage: authoritative about intent, never
about the corpus.

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / Decision · hash: sha256:ba65fe3778cae9bbf2ffa480b6dc3cfd8b6b7e10d604baa44a0f9b95e4fa2ff3*

Two rules follow, and both are mechanical rather than advisory.

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / Decision · hash: sha256:a37dcc5a892ac5213e3a41894533db7496d4b3023896dd40e7bd671348b65b63*

**1. Where the plan and the corpus disagree, the corpus wins and the plan's figure is
recorded, not deleted.** The register at `tests/corpus/families/counts.json` carries the
measured value, the extraction that produced it, the corpus it was measured over, and the
plan's figure marked `superseded` with a reading of what that figure actually counted. A
number that is quietly replaced leaves the next reader unable to tell a correction from a
transcription error, and leaves the plan looking wrong where it was merely counting
something else.

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / Decision · hash: sha256:8b47b97d9acd005fac010c5d8375b03a276a97b2b679d283f5e50bb8db3ed285*

**2. Every count Nomos asserts names its unit and its corpus.** A count without an
executable extraction is not a measurement, so each register entry has an extractor in
`family_counts.rs` and an entry with none fails the suite. The sentence in the register is
that extractor's reading, not a substitute for it.

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / Consequences · hash: sha256:89452c3c3f042e75cb1c74f2df2a941f9dbbbad6127f3d11c1fb606337059416*

## Consequences

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / Consequences · hash: sha256:e29b30eedb6645cfb63e3a5e04625fb862b43c5991b13479ea3b5d08f333e24e*

The register is the single home for these numbers. A restoration, a regression report or a
projection quotes it rather than re-deriving, and the store's own row census answers the
same three questions — pipe lines, authored rows, data rows — as three queries over a typed
column rather than one number and two subtractions.

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / Consequences · hash: sha256:edba5d5b82df098500faf61a537cb9fe06617bf4aac82b1a55a592a91812792e*

A count can be wrong in both directions, and the register is where that becomes visible.
The canonical domain model is the case: 30 is the pipe-line count, the table holds 28 data
rows, and those rows name 38 models because nine of them name more than one. The register
first carried 28 as "domain models" — a row count wearing the name of the thing the rows
list — and the restoration is what found it, because `ModelUsageObservation` shares a row
with `CostObservation` and could not resolve individually until the two were told apart.
The register now carries all three numbers with the extraction that produced each.

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / Consequences · hash: sha256:d3aee2f64df74a397637ea530421cc9eec0c713faaca8d5f376e81674c6aa8d3*

One figure survives as unreproducible and is recorded that way. No extraction over v14.36
yields the plan's **54 service descriptions**: section 6 of volume 02 holds 56 headings at
every depth, 51 of them leaves, 40 of those naming a `Service`, and the section's subsystem
table adds 29 rows. Naming it unreproducible costs nothing; choosing whichever definition
happened to reach 54 would have produced a measurement that agrees with an expectation
instead of with the corpus, which is the failure this record exists to prevent.

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / Consequences · hash: sha256:5d7175c30341dbfce4aae47b92c4764c52ebeef88b4fc22abe5110a02353b121*

This does not license editing the plan. The plan is the approved statement of intent and
stays as written; the disagreement lives in the register, where it is data.

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / What this is not · hash: sha256:212a4060c8bdd7cd4acf80f966c57451306243353e042a860acdffb0ff238632*

## What this is not

### docs/records/D-132-the-plan-is-a-game-plan.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The plan is a game plan, so a count that disagrees with the corpus is superseded, not corrected / What this is not · hash: sha256:dad881ae05600d2d6a4dbd5a95b6190ec1ad740edae251180be3b248725acdc1*

Not a second home for `OD-SPEC-002`, which decided what the regression headline reports for
two specific families and remains the authority on that. This decides the rule that made
both of those the same finding, so the next one is resolved by rule instead of by argument.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#1

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer · hash: sha256:7b64f622caa1e109d4b8b847bedd95201395f46055f521e4923b68e3705d4f7d*

# The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Context · hash: sha256:37861e2e14013ad7c69dfa0ecab17370a0a0e6cf9631382cdc23dff2fa1ba904*

## Context

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Context · hash: sha256:9afcd39ec4325a238b73a9433c476766ae04a46df08996ed934a4d420b270833*

Four phases built a content-addressed store, a preservation ledger, a bundle round trip and
fourteen projection profiles. The `nomos` binary had one group, `work`, and did not depend
on any specification crate. Phase 2's stated payoff — ask what the canonical domain model
said, verbatim, and get the real rows — was not answerable from a command line, and the
fourteen renderers had never been run by anything but their own tests.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Context · hash: sha256:4cdd27353c9037c595dd91a2e50bcbdcaf1bbecf5b2e68e4670687eee74e7a10*

Building the group forced a question the tree had no answer to: *which store does a read
command open?* Nothing persists one. Every `SpecificationStore` in this workspace is
`In_Memory`, built inside a test and dropped at the end of it. There is no database file, no
command that produces one, and `OD-SPEC-001` deliberately leaves the backend question open
while naming the JSONL bundle rather than the database as the portable authority.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Context · hash: sha256:5bb0870e23b3273122a7e7b822259efaa83879e89d39d0ca409758db0075af05*

The second question is worse, and it is `OD-GATE-001`'s finding one level up. Most of what
this system is about lives in the v14 authoring corpus, which is not in this repository and
is not on most machines. A read command over a store the corpus never reached returns
nothing — and nothing is exactly what it returns when the identifier is genuinely unknown.
The two answers are opposite. One means *configure a corpus*; the other means *you have the
wrong identifier*. They printed the same.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Decision · hash: sha256:a15c7c13f167e5ac9204c02acb3f22d9fffdadf996618ee0e068a4b27e4c1511*

## Decision

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Decision · hash: sha256:6383a32dd0dfc8f3991b3ae1b7e95be5c50069e3d532bbd2ed3d8c4eefafe8bc*

**The store is assembled per invocation, from two layers.** This repository's governing
records are embedded in the binary and seeded unconditionally, so a machine with no corpus
can still ask what Nomos decided about itself. The v14 corpus is layered over them when
`--corpus` or `NOMOS_V14_CORPUS` names one. Nothing is written to disk; there is no cache,
no build step and no store file that can be stale.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Decision · hash: sha256:efbbf9d45a1faec362214cb1aec0ec689165f3b76436259634395946d591921f*

Measured rather than assumed: assembling the whole corpus — 10 domain volumes, 2,533 blocks,
493 normative statements, 2,619 catalog nodes — takes about 0.2 s, and the embedded records
alone about 0.02 s. At that cost a store nobody has to remember to rebuild is worth more than
one that answers faster and can disagree with the corpus it came from.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Decision · hash: sha256:e04dc17ffa2ce247e387c3bce6d6d376512a1e57a32084f53d8d92582451592e*

**An absence is a value, not a smaller answer.** Every source that was expected and not read
produces a record naming four things: what is missing, where it was looked for, why it is not
there, and *what is consequently not in this store*. The fourth is the one a reader would
never think to ask for, and it is the one that stops a short answer from reading as a
complete one. A command whose answer is empty because something was missing says so and exits
`6`; `1` means the store is whole and does not hold it. Those are two different next actions
and they get two different codes.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Decision · hash: sha256:9bf80c824ee796f1f3f67d4fcc05ddd37f26dff4bd261e4aeeff8bd16a06d169*

This applies to rendering as well as to reading. `nomos-spec-project` already refuses to
render a section that selected nothing, and its message — declare `may_be_empty` if nothing is
the honest answer — is right over a whole store and wrong over one the corpus never reached,
where it sends a reader to edit a profile because of a variable that is not set. So an empty
section over an incomplete store is reported as the absence instead.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Decision · hash: sha256:14e16973fc569029a4a0fe106ec30854515d883df0b5d2847d71e6c72a81b361*

**Content goes to standard output and everything about it goes to standard error.** So
`nomos spec record --id D-129 > D-129.md` writes the record's bytes and nothing else, and the
file it produces hashes to what the store holds. A header line mixed into the content would
make "verbatim" a claim about the interesting part of the output rather than about the output.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Decision · hash: sha256:58e69005a70bec1ed3bcf9bd1b9e167131f654b8d66d03144c639850130ecbec*

**The commands are exercised by running the built binary.** The libraries under them have
been covered since Phase 1; the part that had never run once was argument parsing — the
dispatch from `argv`, the flags, the exit codes and which stream each answer goes to. A test
that calls `Run` directly proves none of that, because it is the caller that assembled the
command.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Consequences · hash: sha256:89452c3c3f042e75cb1c74f2df2a941f9dbbbad6127f3d11c1fb606337059416*

## Consequences

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Consequences · hash: sha256:0343ac5bd4cee0c02d179aac5223672c742e0e4443ce729ce0e6ac639d669145*

`nomos-cli` now names three specification crates. It is a composition root at band 90 and the
only place permitted to: the spec system sits beside the kernel rather than above it, and
nothing in the product may reach it directly.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Consequences · hash: sha256:0817acf51a22d8762cd8c251f91d5c0e0a8458282ca4749b13cad2067380f2be*

The corpus variable is read in exactly one place — `main.rs` — and handed to the assembler as
data, together with the name it came from so an absence can say how to supply one. That is
what lets the whole read surface, absences included, be exercised on a machine that has no
corpus at all.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Consequences · hash: sha256:fa7bca03295fa00fb9eb8f58da8e256182b8038eb4f4ec1c266c5bb32778aa39*

`crates/host/nomos-cli/tests/read_surface.rs` runs the binary sixteen times and reads no
corpus: it removes the variable from the child's environment so a machine that has one
behaves like a machine that does not, and builds a two-row corpus of its own where one is
wanted. It is therefore not one of the sixty-eight gates `OD-GATE-001` counts, and it
assembles the variable's name with `concat!` for the reason that file does — a test that names
a corpus variable without reading a corpus would inflate the measured hole rather than
measure it.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:4824749d250c30ac7d0d3b75dd866d8a845308adcba154f5372cf74980c63d83*

## Alternatives Considered

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:774279a1e4f80895c390c7bbc90ef1b678bae08f72665b10eac41b772af4419b*

**Persist a database and have `spec` open it.** Rejected. Nothing builds one, so the first
command anybody ran would fail with instructions to run a command that does not exist; and a
store file is a fourth copy of the corpus that can silently disagree with the three that
already exist. The bundle, not the database, is this system's portable authority.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:19a42b2ce5d4d7158ca5562c07ac8611b81476962d03dc35525f7b8a9a7ad51d*

**Report a missing corpus as an empty result.** Rejected, and it is the defect this record
exists to prevent. Sixty-eight tests already report `ok` having read nothing; a read surface
that prints an empty table for a corpus it never had is the same defect wearing a different
hat.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / Alternatives Considered · hash: sha256:0efb18d15dfdd6a020642a4068a2c3f6dc8501f48ba724717adcec3b0e682080*

**Fail when no corpus is configured.** Rejected. The governing records are embedded and there
are real questions answerable without a corpus — every one of this repository's own decisions
is one. A command that can never succeed on most machines is a command everybody learns to
work around, which is the mutually-contradictory-gate defect `rustfmt.toml` already records.

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / What This Is Not · hash: sha256:8c096e9ff713a2d91679182618fcba53119b00032e6e47e091a14b7e89a7235f*

## What This Is Not

### docs/records/D-133-the-read-surface-assembles-its-store-and-names-what-is-missing.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: The read surface assembles its store on every invocation, and an absence is not an empty answer / What This Is Not · hash: sha256:291dbb21210bb2731db602a5588b5967c22d07a564b77a15f71e03de5cd35096*

Not the authoring round trip. `D-129` decides that a record can be read out as markdown *and
the edit written back* as a transaction with a mandatory preview. This builds the first half
only, over a store that is still seeded from files. `P9-AUTHORING` carries the rest, and
nothing here should be read as narrowing it.
